large vision-language models (LVLMs) have been adopted as automated evaluators of text-image pairs, enabling nuanced assessments that capture semantic coherence beyond superficial matching.
Each LVLM judge is prompted with a standardized evaluation instruction alongside a text-image pair.

traditional metrics such as Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS) have been widely adopted. Embedding-based methods, including CLIPScore and BLIPScore, have improved evaluation by leveraging pretrained vision-language models to compute crossmodal similarity.
Each LVLM judge is prompted with a standardized evaluation instruction alongside a text-image pair.

the LLM-as-a-judge paradigm has gained popularity, offering scalable and consistent evaluations. However, these models have been shown to be vulnerable to biases and adversarial attacks. Recently, this paradigm has been extended to multimodal scenarios through LVLM-as-a-judge frameworks.
